We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Preview 7. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/preview7).

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git and Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Improper removal of sensitive information before storage or transfer in .NET allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sourcelink/issues/1757 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-212: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transfer ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### Published NuGet packages Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 The affected packages used by .NET 8 and .NET 9 SDKs are built with SDK-specific prerelease versions that aren't published as stable NuGet packages. Update to SDK 8.0.130 or 8.0.424, SDK 9.0.120 or 9.0.317, or SDK 10.0.111 or 10.0.303 to receive the fix. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-62900](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-62900) ### Acknowledgements Ivan Demchuk ### Revisions V1.0 (08/11/2026): Advisory published.

## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Windows Presentation Foundation. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Events.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "optimize shadow copy from .nuget/packages" (#13863) at dotnet/roslyn
Events.RelatedBody:
**Version Used**: any

**Steps to Reproduce**: 
1. open VS
2. open roslyn.sln

We shadow copy analyzers to the temp directory. When the dlls originate in .nuget/packages we can skip the IO cost of copying because the package is immutable.

@mavasani 
"We can surely tune our shadow copy based analyzer assembly loader to handle this special case, as long as we are guaranteeing this part for the nuget cache folder: “The reason is it’s supposed to be immutable and we can save the cost of disk copies if we just load it from the original location”. Note that we will lock the file on the disk so user might possibly not even be able to delete analyzer packages until the VS session consuming them is closed."

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs " (#1775)

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

Best Regards,

Raphael

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: submit all helix jobs at once
Issues.Body:
Now that the helix test jobs only submit to helix and do not wait for completion, we can instead run a single job that submits all the test configurations to helix.  This reduces the number of AzDo machines we have to acquire.

However - it does mean that the stage / phase names change which breaks test history lookup (would conflate tests with the same name that run in multiple test configurations).  To fix that we derive a stable name for the test configuration based on the RunTests parameters that we use when submitting the run to helix.  Then we can query AzDo for tests matching that run name when looking for test history to scope them to only tests for that test configuration.

Issues.Title: Add manually triggered stage for publishing prerelease roslyn-language-server packages
Issues.Body:
Adds an approval-gated, manually triggered stage to the official build that publishes prerelease `roslyn-language-server` packages to NuGet.org using trusted publishing (WIF/OIDC), with a WhatIf mode enabled by default.

### `azure-pipelines-official.yml`
- New boolean parameter `PublishPrereleaseRoslynLspWhatIf` (`WhatIf Publish Prerelease Roslyn LSP`), defaulting to `true` so initial runs validate without publishing.
- New `publish_prerelease_roslyn_lsp` stage with `trigger: manual`, placed immediately after `build` so it picks up the implicit dependency. `insert` keeps its explicit `dependsOn: build`, so insertion is not blocked by the manual stage.
- Deployment job on the `roslyn-nuget-publishing-approvers` environment (approval checks configured externally), internal Linux 1ES pool, `checkout: self`, and `DownloadBuildArtifacts@1` of `PackageArtifacts` into `$(Pipeline.Workspace)`.
- Token exchange runs in both modes so the WIF connection and NuGet.org policy are exercised in WhatIf. The API key is passed to the script via `NUGET_API_KEY` rather than an argument.

### `eng/pipelines/steps/get-nuget-api-key.yml` (new)
- Steps-only (1ES-safe) template: `AzureCLI@2` + bash acquires an Entra ID token for the gallery audience, masks it, and exchanges it at `POST {gallery}/api/v2/token` for a short-lived API key exposed as the secret variable `NuGetApiKey`.
- `discoveryOnly: true` decodes the JWT payload and prints only `tid`/`oid` — the values needed to register the trusted publishing policy — and exits without requesting a key.
- Response body lives only in an agent temp file removed by a cleanup trap; neither token nor key is logged.

### `scripts/publish-prerelease-roslyn-lsp.ps1` (new)
- `SupportsShouldProcess` so standard `-WhatIf`/`-Confirm` work; locally invokable under PowerShell 7.
- Scans only the root of `PackageDirectory` for `roslyn-language-server.*.nupkg` (symbol packages excluded), parses the version from the filename, and requires a hyphen so stable versions cannot be published by this path.
- Pushes with `--skip-duplicate` to tolerate retries/partial publication; an API key is only required outside WhatIf.

```powershell
./scripts/publish-prerelease-roslyn-lsp.ps1 -PackageDirectory ./artifacts/packages/Release -WhatIf
# Validated package 'roslyn-language-server.5.11.0-1.26412.5.nupkg'
#   Id: roslyn-language-server
#   Version: 5.11.0-1.26412.5
# Validation completed for 1 package(s). No packages were published because -WhatIf was specified.
```

Issues.Title: [ProjectData] Reassess recoverable I/O handling after ownership transfer
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Reassess ProjectData recoverable-I/O helpers against Roslyn `IOUtilities` patterns.

## Background

ProjectData currently uses operation-specific exception filters and a local `IsRecoverableCacheReadException` helper. PR #84790 review suggested considering Roslyn `IOUtilities`:

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/84790#discussion_r3732200129

## Proposed work

- Audit ProjectData filesystem catch filters.
- Determine whether `IOUtilities` can be used without an undesirable Workspaces dependency.
- Prefer the local helper when using `IOUtilities` would broaden catches, hide diagnostics, or add a heavyweight dependency.
- Keep specialized XML, JSON, cryptographic, and process exception policies operation-specific.

## Completion criteria

- Recoverable exception policy is consistent and documented.
- No broad catch masks programming errors or cancellation.
- The ProjectData dependency boundary remains intentional.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[ProjectData] Reassess recoverable I/O handling after ownership transfer" (#84863)

Issues.Title: [ProjectData] Adopt Roslyn temporary-directory test helpers after ownership transfer
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Migrate the ProjectData tests from custom temporary-directory fixtures to Roslyn test infrastructure.

## Background

PR #84790 review identified several tests using `Path.GetTempPath()`, custom `IDisposable` fixtures, and silent `Directory.Delete` cleanup:

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/84790#discussion_r3732033795

## Proposed work

- Use Roslyn `TempRoot`/`TempDirectory` helpers for ProjectData filesystem fixtures.
- Replace repeated custom temporary pack/root lifetime implementations where the Roslyn helpers preserve the required directory shape.
- Remove silent cleanup implementations owned solely by these fixtures.
- Preserve tests that require explicit environment-variable restoration or specialized filesystem behavior.

## Completion criteria

- ProjectData tests use Roslyn temporary-file infrastructure where appropriate.
- Fixture cleanup and environment restoration remain deterministic.
- Existing filesystem and cross-platform scenarios remain covered.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[ProjectData] Adopt Roslyn temporary-directory test helpers after ownership transfer" (#84862)

Issues.Title: [ProjectData] Evaluate Roslyn pooled collections in the schema generator after ownership transfer
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Evaluate whether `Microsoft.NET.ProjectData.Generators` should adopt Roslyn pooled collections.

## Background

PR #84790 review raised the opportunity to use Roslyn pooled types in the schema generator:

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/84790#discussion_r3731990367

## Proposed work

- Measure or otherwise identify repeated build-time allocations worth optimizing.
- Reassess suitable uses of `ArrayBuilder<T>`, `PooledDictionary<TKey, TValue>`, `PooledHashSet<T>`, and `PooledStringBuilder`.
- Adopt pooling only where the benefit justifies the additional lifetime and disposal complexity.
- Keep standard collections where the schema is too small for pooling to matter.

## Completion criteria

- The allocation tradeoff is documented.
- Any pooling change has focused tests and correct lifetime handling.
- Generated output remains equivalent.

Issues.Title: Add HAA0304: local function converted to a delegate captures variables
Issues.Body:
Closes dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#1438.

**Depends on #84858** and is stacked on its branch — the three pinned gap tests added there are flipped here. Please merge #84858 first; I'll rebase onto `main` once it lands.

### Why a new ID

Per maintainer guidance in the linked discussion, HAA0301/HAA0302 are not extended — that would start reporting on code that is green for existing users. HAA0304 is the next free ID in the closure family.

### Before / after

```csharp
[PerformanceSensitive("uri")]
public void SomeMethod()
{
    int local = 1;
    void LocalFunction() => Console.WriteLine(local);

    LocalFunction();               // no diagnostic, before and after — see below
    Action action = LocalFunction; // before: HAA0603 only
                                   // after:  HAA0603 + HAA0304 "…local function 'LocalFunction' Captures: local"
}
```

### Why direct calls are not flagged

When a local function is only ever invoked directly, the compiler emits its captured state as a by-ref struct passed to the callee — the closure lives on the stack and nothing reaches the heap. Flagging it would be a false positive. Converting the method group to a delegate is what forces that state into a heap-allocated display class, so the rule triggers at the conversion, never at the call.

### Where it lives

The descriptor is in `DisplayClassAllocationAnalyzer` rather than a sibling analyzer, because this package ties rule-ID families to analyzer types — `HAA03xx` is that analyzer throughout `AnalyzerReleases`, the `.sarif` (`typeName`), and the generated `.md`. Detection is a self-contained private method, so the existing lambda code paths are untouched.

### Detection

The check runs at the reference site, which covers every conversion position through one code path — initializer, assignment, argument, and return. The return position matters: HAA0603 is *never* reported there (`ReturnStatementExpressionCheck` only tests for boxing), so HAA0304 cannot lean on any overlap. Both `IdentifierName` and `GenericName` are handled, so generic local functions are not missed.

Captures come from `AnalyzeDataFlow` on the local function statement, mirroring the existing closure analysis. Analyzing the statement rather than the body is what makes the local function count as a capturing function inside the analyzed region. Variables declared inside the local function are filtered out, so a nested lambda capturing one of the local function's own locals does not produce a false positive — that display class is allocated as the local function runs, whether or not it was ever converted to a delegate.

HAA0603 is untouched and coexists, exactly as it already does with HAA0301 for lambdas — #84858's HAA0603 tests are unchanged here, which is the proof.

Note that `new Action(LocalFunction)` does report HAA0304, even though HAA0603 deliberately skips explicit delegate creation (that allocation is HAA0502's job). The closure allocation there is real and otherwise unreported. Happy to suppress it if reviewers would rather keep parity with HAA0603's skip.

### `AllowCaptures`

`PerformanceSensitiveAttribute.AllowCaptures` is parsed into `PerformanceSensitiveInfo` but is not read by any analyzer in this package today, and it defaults to `true`, so it currently has no effect on any rule. HAA0304 ignores it too, consistent with HAA0301/HAA0302. Wiring it up — for HAA0304 alone or family-wide — is a behavior change to existing rules and is offered as a follow-up if reviewers want it.

### Tests

135/135 in the package.

Reports HAA0304: capturing local function converted in initializer, assignment, argument, return, generic form, and inside a loop.

Reports nothing: non-capturing local functions in both initializer and return position, direct invocation, `nameof`, a local function whose only capture belongs to itself, and a compilation where `Roslyn.Utilities.PerformanceSensitiveAttribute` is not defined.

A capture of only `this` reports and names `this`, mirroring the lambda behavior pinned in #84858.

### Housekeeping

`AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md` entry added; `.resx` strings added and the 13 `.xlf` files refreshed by the build's xlf pipeline (`state="new"`). The rule listings (`Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PerformanceSensitiveAnalyzers.md`, `.sarif`, `RulesMissingDocumentation.md`) were regenerated with the repo's `GenerateAnalyzerConfigAndDocumentationFiles` target, and the CI validate-only mode of that target passes.

Issues.Title: Add characterization tests for closure allocation analysis of local functions
Issues.Body:
Step 1 of 2 for dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#1438. Tests only — no production code changes.

Before adding a new rule for local functions that get converted to delegates, this pins the current behavior of the closure analyzers so the follow-up diff shows exactly what changes. Per maintainer guidance in the linked discussion, HAA0301/HAA0302 will not be extended (that would break existing users); a new rule HAA0304 follows in a separate PR.

### `DisplayClassAllocationAnalyzer` (HAA0301/HAA0302)

- lambda capturing a local → HAA0301 + HAA0302
- `static` lambda → no diagnostics
- lambda capturing only `this` → HAA0301 names `this`; HAA0302 lands on the enclosing method identifier
- nested lambdas capturing one outer local → capture reported once per enclosing lambda
- local function invoked directly → no diagnostics (correct: captured state is a by-ref struct, no heap allocation)
- capturing local function converted to a delegate (initializer, argument, return) → nothing reported today, although a display class *is* allocated. Documents the gap tracked by dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#1438; HAA0304 will cover it.

### `TypeConversionAllocationAnalyzer` (HAA0603)

- HAA0603 fires for initializer and argument positions, for capturing and non-capturing local functions alike
- HAA0603 does *not* fire for a returned method group — the return path only checks boxing conversions
- direct invocation reports nothing

Full `PerformanceSensitiveAnalyzers` suite: 126/126 passing.

Issues.Title: Add tag for diagnostics that need to be suppressed with `[UnconditionalSuppressMessage]`.
Issues.Body:
## Background and Motivation

Some analyzers like the trimming and AOT compatibility analyzers, emit diagnostics that would also be emitted by external tools, and therefore would require `[UnconditionalSuppressMessage]` in order for them to be suppressed. However, suppressing them from the IDE generates either a `#pragma warning disable`, a `[SuppressMessage]` or changes to the `.editorconfig`, none of which will be seen by the external tool.

I am proposing a new entry in the `WellKnownDiagnosticTags` class, that will instruct IDEs to suppress diagnostics tagged with it using `[UnconditionalSuppressMessage]`. Additionally:

* IDEs will _not_ suggest suppressing the diagnostic with `#pragma warning disable`, or configuring its severity in the `.editorconfig`.
  * If `UnconditionalSuppressMessageAttribute` is not available, we can either ignore the tag, or not suggest suppressing the diagnostic at all.
* Optionally, we can report a warning if the user attempts to do any of the above, indicating that the suppression will not be entirely effective.

## Proposed API

```diff
namespace Microsoft.CodeAnalysis
{
     public static WellKnownDiagnosticTags
     {
+        public const string RequiresUnconditionalSuppression = nameof(RequiresUnconditionalSuppression);
     }
}
```

## Usage Examples

<!--
Please provide code examples that highlight how the proposed API additions are meant to be consumed.
This will help suggest whether the API has the right shape to be functional, performant and useable.
You can use code blocks like this:
-->

``` C#
// some lines of code here
```

## Alternative Designs

<!--
Were there other options you considered, such as alternative API shapes?
How does this compare to analogous APIs in other ecosystems and libraries?
-->

## Risks

None that I can think of. Roslyn already recognizes `[UnconditionalSuppressMessage]`; this proposal adds better IDE integration for it.

Issues.Title: Update Issue Monster workflow lock file
Issues.Body: Updates the generated Issue Monster workflow lock file after #55759 changed the source workflow's \skip-if-match.max\ value from 2 to 80. This makes the runnable workflow use the intended limit.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Update Issue Monster workflow lock file" (#55760)

Issues.Title: Allow Copilot assignment even if >= 2 issues are assigned to Copilot
Issues.Body:
The limit for 'skip-if-match' is meant to help prevent the possibility of accidental assignment to too many copilot issues, and also to prevent the issuer assigner from overwhelming engineers with PRs.

This is different from the limit on how many assignments can be sent out at a time, which is dispatch-workflow: max, which is already `3`.

Right now, we have quite a few https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pulls/@copilot copilot PRs so this limit unintentionally blocks the issue monster. Those existing PRs are not from the issue-monster but individuals.

`2` is clearly too low of a limit and blocking the assigner from running at all, as observed in https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/31646249249 - `80` seems reasonable for now to unblock but I will own revisiting this if we are not attentive to the PRs generated.

Issues.Title: [aw] Detection Runs
Issues.Body:
This issue tracks all runs where threat detection flagged problems in agentic workflows in this repository. Each workflow run that completes with a detection warning or failure posts a comment here.

<details>
<summary>What is a Detection Problem?</summary>

A detection problem occurs when the threat detection system either:
- **Detects potential security threats** (prompt injection, secret leak, malicious patch)
- **Fails to produce results** (agent failure, parse error)

When `continue-on-error: true` (the default), these problems produce warnings and safe outputs still proceed. When `continue-on-error: false`, they block safe outputs entirely.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How This Helps</summary>

This issue helps you:
- Track workflows where threat detection raised concerns
- Review patterns of detection warnings or failures
- Identify false positives or recurring issues with threat detection
- Monitor the health of the threat detection system

</details>

<details>
<summary>Resources</summary>

- [GitHub Agentic Workflows Documentation](https://github.com/github/gh-aw)

</details>

> [!TIP]
> To configure threat detection behavior, update the frontmatter:
> ```yaml
> safe-outputs:
>   threat-detection:
>     continue-on-error: true   # Warnings only (default)
>     # continue-on-error: false  # Strict mode — block safe outputs
> ```

---

> This issue is automatically managed by GitHub Agentic Workflows. Do not close this issue manually.
>
> **No action to take** - Do not assign to an agent.

Issues.Title: Add end-to-end MSBuild telemetry coverage
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- add a hermetic OTLP HTTP/protobuf receiver and host matrix for cold/hot MSBuild servers, in-process builds, server fallback, and opt-out
- keep the MSBuild activity open until logger shutdown so the final build event is exported
- force-flush without shutting down providers between persistent-server builds, with full cleanup at process exit
- create a fallback activity when telemetry is tracked without an ambient activity

## Testing

- targeted TelemetryHostMatrixTests, GivenMSBuildLogger, and standalone-activity coverage (16 tests)

Part of #55749. The contract/snapshot gate described as item 3 remains a separate follow-up, as allowed by the issue's per-item PR split.

Issues.Title: Make telemetry testable and guide contributors to test new events
Issues.Body:
# Summary

The MSBuild server discards its build telemetry. The tests do not find this condition. A contributor who adds a new telemetry event gets no signal to test it.

I reproduced the error locally. The next section gives the measurement.

This issue asks for three work items:

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A test harness collects real telemetry from a child `dotnet` process. It uses the Aspire dashboard. |
| 2 | Tests use the harness for each host. The MSBuild server is one host. |
| 3 | A contract file and a CI gate tell the contributors to test each new event. |

Item 3 is the most important item for the contributors. It changes the test from a convention into a condition of the build.

An optional item 4 is at the end of this description.

# The verified reproduction

**SDK:** `11.0.100-preview.7.26357.101` (a build from 2026-07-07, before the correction in PR #55582).

**Collector:** the Aspire dashboard, version 13.4.6.

```
dotnet tool install -g Aspire.Cli --version 13.4.6

aspire dashboard run --frontend-url http://127.0.0.1:18889 ^
                     --otlp-http-url http://127.0.0.1:14319 ^
                     --allow-anonymous --non-interactive --nologo
```

Each trial used these steps:

1. Run `dotnet build-server shutdown`. This step removes each MSBuild process of a previous trial.
2. Run `dotnet build --no-incremental` with the telemetry variables below.
3. Wait for the export operation. Then read `GET http://127.0.0.1:18889/api/telemetry/spans?limit=1000`.

```
DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=false
DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_ENABLE_EXPORTER=1
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:14319
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf
DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS=15000
```

**The result:**

| Trial | `dotnet/cli/msbuild/build` events | `InitialMSBuildServerState` |
|---|---|---|
| `MSBUILDUSESERVER=0` | **1** | absent |
| `MSBUILDUSESERVER=1` | **0** | no event |

A build without the server also sent these events: `dotnet/cli/msbuild/build/tasks`, `dotnet/cli/msbuild/build/tasks/taskfactory`, `dotnet/cli/msbuild/loggingConfiguration`, and `dotnet/cli/msbuild/targetframeworkeval`.

**The control.** In the trial with the server, these conditions were all true at the same time:

| Observation | Value |
|---|---|
| Exit code of the build | `0`, thus the build was successful |
| MSBuild server process after the build | present, thus the server made the build |
| `dotnet/cli/toplevelparser/command` | received |
| `dotnet/cli/sublevelparser/command` | received |
| `dotnet/cli/command/finish` | received |
| `dotnet/cli/msbuild/build` | **absent** |

The CLI events and the build event use the same process, the same exporter, and the same connection. The CLI events arrived. Thus the export operation is correct, and the network is correct. Only the build event is absent. This control shows that the product discards the event. It does not show an error in the test method.

This result agrees with the data in the backend. The backend contains events from this SDK version, but it contains no event from a build that the server completed.

I also examined `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_DISABLE_TRACE_EXPORT`. This variable is not a cause. Both values of this variable give the same result.

# The cause

The `TelemetryClient.TrackEventTask` method attaches each event to the current activity:

```csharp
var @event = new ActivityEvent($"dotnet/cli/{eventName}", tags: MakeTags(properties));
Activity.Current?.AddEvent(@event);
```

If `Activity.Current` is null, the `?.` operator discards the event. The code shows no error message. The build is successful.

Before PR #55582, `MSBuildLogger` monitored only the `BuildFinished` event and started no activity. The managed CLI process has a current activity, thus its events go to the backend. The MSBuild server process has no current activity, thus it discards its build events.

A build that falls back to an in-process build sends its telemetry, because the client process makes this build. A build that the server completes sends nothing. Thus the dashboards show a fallback rate of almost 100 percent. This rate is not correct.

PR #55231 (2026-07-14) makes the MSBuild server the default for `dotnet build` in .NET 11:

```csharp
private static bool UseMSBuildServer => Env.GetEnvironmentVariableAsBool("DOTNET_CLI_USE_MSBUILD_SERVER", true);
```

Thus the quantity of the lost data increased after this date. PR #55582 corrected the error on 2026-08-07. No test in CI failed during this period.

# The limits of the current tests

**`FakeTelemetry`** (`test/dotnet.Tests/CommandTests/MSBuild/FakeTelemetry.cs`) shows that the logger called a method. It does not show that the process sent data.

**The tests in PR #55582** examine the parent of the activity. They use a synthetic `IEventSource`. They do not start a build. They do not start a server.

**The disk log** (`DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_LOG_PATH` with `TelemetryDiskLogger`) is the only method that examines real output. But it uses `AddInMemoryExporter(s_activities)`. The product uses `AddOtlpExporter` or `AddAzureMonitorTraceExporter`.

# Item 1: A telemetry test harness with the Aspire dashboard

Do not write a collector. The Aspire dashboard receives OTLP and gives a query API. Thus this team owns fewer parts.

I verified each step of this method with the commands in the reproduction section above.

Create `test/dotnet.Tests/TelemetryTests/TelemetryCollectorFixture.cs`. The class does these operations:

1. It starts the Aspire dashboard as a child process. It uses `--allow-anonymous`, thus a test needs no API key.
2. It selects a free port for the frontend and a free port for OTLP. Two tests in parallel then use different ports.
3. It gives the OTLP endpoint address to the test.
4. It reads `GET /api/telemetry/spans` and returns the events of each span.
5. It stops the dashboard at the end of the test class.

The response is OTLP JSON. `System.Text.Json` reads it. The `events` array of each span contains a `name` and an `attributes` array. This structure is the structure that the SDK sends. Thus a test examines the event name and each tag name. A decoder for the protobuf format is not necessary.

Give the fixture this API:

```csharp
IReadOnlyList<CollectedEvent> events = await fixture.GetEventsAsync();
events.Where(e => e.Name == "dotnet/cli/msbuild/build").Should().ContainSingle();
```

`CollectedEvent` contains the name and a dictionary of the tags.

Use the `PersistentStorageTelemetryE2ETests.cs` file as the example for the child process. Use `SdkTest`, `TestAssetsManager`, and `DotnetCommand` in the same manner.

## About the dependency

The Aspire dashboard is a tool. It is not a package reference of a test project. The command `dotnet tool install -g Aspire.Cli --version 13.4.6` installs it in some seconds. Thus this method adds no assembly to the product or to the tests.

These tests do not operate on a source-build leg. Thus the acquisition of the tool is acceptable. Exclude these tests from each leg that has no network access.

# Item 2: Tests for each host

Create `test/dotnet.Tests/TelemetryTests/TelemetryHostMatrixTests.cs`.

Use a matrix of the hosts. A list of conditions becomes old. A matrix shows which host has no test.

| Host | Environment | The test examines this |
|---|---|---|
| MSBuild server, cold start | default settings, no server operates | One `dotnet/cli/msbuild/build` event. `InitialMSBuildServerState` is `cold`. |
| MSBuild server, hot start | default settings, second build | One event. `InitialMSBuildServerState` is `hot`. Not zero events. Not two events. |
| In process | `MSBUILDUSESERVER=0` | One event. `InitialMSBuildServerState` is absent. |
| Fall back to in process | a condition that stops the server | One event. `ServerFallbackReason` has a value. |
| Opt out | `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1` | Zero events. |

In .NET 11 the server is the default. Thus a test that sets `MSBUILDUSESERVER` manually does not test the path that most customers use. Use the default settings for the first two rows.

## Two conditions from the reproduction

These two conditions are necessary. Without them a test gives a false result.

**1. Run `dotnet build-server shutdown` before each trial.** An MSBuild process of a previous trial stays in memory. This process keeps the environment of its own trial. Thus it sends the telemetry to the wrong address, or it sends nothing. My first three trials gave a false result for this reason.

**2. Examine a control event in the same trial.** A build sends `dotnet/cli/toplevelparser/command` and `dotnet/cli/command/finish` from the CLI process. Assert that these events are present. This assertion separates two conditions:

- The build did not operate, or the export did not operate. Then the control events are also absent.
- The build operated and the export operated, but the product discarded the build event. Then the control events are present.

The second condition is the error in this issue. Without the control, a test cannot show the difference.

Write the assertions one time in a private method. Then each host is one row and not a new test.

# Item 3: A contract file and a CI gate

This item tells the contributors to test their new events.

Today a contributor gets no signal. The `documentation/project-docs/telemetry.md` file says: "Ensure that all telemetry events and properties are accurately documented". This is a convention. No code makes this necessary.

## The contract file

Use the `Verify.MSTest` package. This repository already references it in `test/dotnet.Tests/dotnet.Tests.csproj`. The `test/dotnet.Tests/CommandTests/Test/snapshots/MTPHelpSnapshotTests.VerifyMTPHelpOutput.verified.txt` file is an example of a snapshot.

Create `test/dotnet.Tests/TelemetryTests/TelemetryContractTests.cs` and its snapshot file. The test uses the harness of item 1. The OTLP JSON contains each tag name, thus the test needs no other source. The snapshot contains each event name and each tag name in sequence:

```
dotnet/cli/msbuild/build
  BuildCheckEnabled
  BuildEngineHost
  BuildSuccess
  BuildTarget
  InitialMSBuildServerState
  ProjectPath
  ServerEnableReason
  ServerFallbackReason
dotnet/cli/msbuild/loggingConfiguration
  ConsoleLogger
  TerminalLogger
```

The test removes the values, because a value is not stable. Then `Verify` compares the result with the snapshot file.

## The static check

`MSBuildLogger.cs` declares 16 constants with the `EventName` suffix. `TargetFrameworkTelemetryEventName` is an example.

Add a test that reads these constants with reflection. The test compares them with the contract file. This check finds an event that no test condition sends.

## The three conditions of failure

Each message must tell the contributor the next action:

| Condition | The message |
|---|---|
| The code declares an event. The contract file does not contain it. | "The event `dotnet/cli/foo` is not in the contract file. Add a test condition that sends this event. Then accept the new snapshot." |
| The contract file contains an event. No test sends it. | "No test sends the event `dotnet/cli/foo`. Add a test condition, or remove the event from the contract file." |
| A tag name or its letter case changed. | "The tag `BuildSuccess` changed to `buildSuccess`. This change stops the queries in the backend. Confirm that this change is necessary." |

The third condition is important. A change to a tag name causes no error in the code. But it stops each query that uses this tag.

## The documentation

Add a section to `documentation/project-docs/telemetry.md`. Give this instruction to a contributor who adds an event:

1. Add the event name as a constant.
2. Add a test condition to `TelemetryHostMatrixTests` that sends the event.
3. Run the tests. Accept the new snapshot file.
4. Add the event to the table in this document.

# Item 4 (optional): Make the error visible in the code

The items above examine the known events and the known hosts. This item protects the hosts that we do not know today. The AOT CLI and `dotnet watch` are examples.

Change `TrackEventTask`. Do one of these two operations:

- Write a diagnostic message when no current activity is present. Use `Debug.Fail` in the debug build.
- Let `TelemetryClient` start its own activity when no current activity is present. Then the host operates correctly.

The second operation is better.

# Acceptance criteria

Each item can be a separate pull request.

**Item 1**

- [ ] `TelemetryCollectorFixture` starts the Aspire dashboard and stops it. It uses free ports.
- [ ] It reads the events and their tags from `GET /api/telemetry/spans`.
- [ ] It adds no package reference to the product or to the test project.
- [ ] One test shows that a `dotnet build` command sends a `dotnet/cli/msbuild/build` event.

**Item 2**

- [ ] `TelemetryHostMatrixTests` contains each row of the table in item 2.
- [ ] Each trial runs `dotnet build-server shutdown` first.
- [ ] Each trial asserts a control event from the CLI process.
- [ ] Use the SDK of the repository. Then a change to the product changes the result of the test.
- [ ] Remove the activity change of PR #55582 from the product code. Then the cold start row and the hot start row must fail. The other rows must stay successful. This criterion shows that the tests find the original error.

**Item 3**

- [ ] The contract snapshot file exists. It contains the events and their tags.
- [ ] A new event without a contract entry causes a failure. The message gives the next action.
- [ ] A changed tag name causes a failure.
- [ ] An event in the contract file that no test sends causes a failure.
- [ ] `telemetry.md` contains the four steps for a contributor.

**Item 4**

- [ ] `TrackEventTask` does not discard an event in silence.
- [ ] A test shows this behavior with no current activity.

# Related items

- PR #55582 corrects the telemetry of the MSBuild server. Item 2 must find such an error.
- PR #53181 and commit `9e81efe746` contain the OTel migration.
- PR #55231 makes the MSBuild server the default.
- PR #55211 changes the exporter to a persist-then-drain design. It also has no end-to-end test.

# Notes

Do not remove `TelemetryDiskLogger`. It is useful for local diagnosis. But it must not be the only test of the real output.

The reproduction above uses an SDK build from before the correction. A new measurement with an SDK build after 2026-08-07 shows the state of the correction in production. This measurement is not in this issue.

Issues.Title: RZ2099 is raised whenever a comment is put inside a [RestrictChildren] tag
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

Having comment tags inside a [RestrictChildren] tag causes the build to fail with RZ2009 error.

### Steps to reproduce

The following markup is causing the issue (using Knockout.js) (partial code)
`<kenora-dropdown button-type="Export" menu-class="scrollable">
    <!-- ko if: someAssert() -->
    <dropdown-header label="Some header" />
    <dropdown-item label="Some label" click-databind="action" visible-databind="assertVisible" />
    <dropdown-divider />
    <!-- /ko -->
</kenora-dropdown>`


### Expected behavior

Comment tags should be ignored by [RestrictChildren]

### Actual behavior

RZ2009 is raised

### Is this a regression?

It was working prior to .NET SDK 10.0.400 installation

### Are there any workarounds?

Rolling back to a previous SDK (didn't test, but it was working with 10.0.301)

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-62900 | .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git and Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Improper removal of sensitive information before storage or transfer in .NET allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sourcelink/issues/1757 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-212: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transfer ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### Published NuGet packages Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 The affected packages used by .NET 8 and .NET 9 SDKs are built with SDK-specific prerelease versions that aren't published as stable NuGet packages. Update to SDK 8.0.130 or 8.0.424, SDK 9.0.120 or 9.0.317, or SDK 10.0.111 or 10.0.303 to receive the fix. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. A tampering vulnerability exists in the .NET SDK (.NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10) container image build process which could allow a local attacker to inject resources that could be incorporated into container images built by other users on the same machine. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/55274 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.0 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-59 (Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 10.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.9 | 10.0.10 ### .NET 9.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.17 | 9.0.18 ### .NET 8.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.28 | 8.0.29 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable nuget package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.29 Runtime or .NET 8.0.129 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.18 Runtime or .NET 9.0.316 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.10 Runtime or .NET 10.0.302 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET XML Encryption (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. A denial of service vulnerability exists in the XML encryption implementation (EncryptedXml) in .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying crafted encrypted XML that causes uncontrolled resource consumption, resulting in denial of service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/130711 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 10.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.9 | 10.0.10 ### .NET 9.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.17 | 9.0.18 ### .NET 8.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.3 | 8.0.4 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable nuget package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.29 Runtime or .NET 8.0.129 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.18 Runtime or .NET 9.0.316 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.10 Runtime or .NET 10.0.302 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.
